P0.8.title: Relay durability (D-7): file-backed store with atomic writes; a restart must lose nothing
P0.8.note: Merged as #57. Persistence is inside the mutation (on disk before put returns) and atomic (temp/fsync/rename/fsync-dir). P0.4 had TWO loss modes: the 10s timer, and writeFileSync truncating the live file so a crash mid-write lost everything rather than 10s. Failed snapshot rolls back and throws; corrupt snapshot quarantines and refuses to boot; RELAY_DUMP_PATH required unless RELAY_EPHEMERAL=1; SIGTERM handled. NOTE: the SIGKILL acceptance test first PASSED against a no-durability build because npx forks the interpreter and killing the wrapper left a grandchild on the port — now spawns the binary directly in its own process group. [E26] split to P0.9 (analysis in infra/relay/README.md), re-verified against merged M9 that the sweeper still needs seconds-precision received_at. G7's 'blocked on P0.8' dependency is now satisfied.

M10.title: Ingest ledger (D-7/M10): capture memories_created[] handles at write time so forget deletes both XTrace scopes instead of reporting skipped
M10.note: Built and verified live: forget now reports 'pool: deleted (2 records)' - the first XTrace deletion this repo has performed. Handles come from the job RESULT so they cannot be captured at write time (the job is pending); the sweeper records them onto the relay entry when the job succeeds and forget reads them back. User scope stays skipped HONESTLY: prose is ingested per batch (M20) so a created memory cannot be attributed to one read_id, and text matching is the fuzzy deletion this task's note forbids. Three bugs found by running rather than testing: the settle-window env var is SETTLE_WINDOW_SECONDS (not CONFIT_-prefixed); forgetPool read the ledger while forgetRelay deleted the entry holding it in one Promise.all; and parseEntry never carried pool_memories inward. The sequencing guard is source-level and says why - three behavioural versions stayed green both ways because in-process JS ordering supplies what the network does not.

G7.title: Rewrite gate zero for D-7: relay survives restart losing nothing, deletion deletes by handle, induction yields a usable claim

It cannot pass and passing would mean nothing. Blocked on P0.8 because claim 1 is durability that does not exist yet. See docs/gate0-results.md and DAG §4 D-3 (amended).

P0.9.title: Close [E26]: the relay's arrival ordering is a side channel now that it holds everything for ever
P0.9.note: Split out of P0.8, which did the durability half. D-7 makes the relay hold every read for ever rather than for minutes, so coarse timestamps move from the [prod] list to required — but neither fix fits inside infra/relay/**. (a) Coarsening received_at changes RelayEntry in src/contracts/types.ts (frozen, integrator only) AND breaks M7's sweeper, which computes a seconds-precision settle window from that exact field; M9 is rewriting the sweeper now, hence the dependency. (b) Requiring the token on GET /reads contradicts P0.4's tested 'reads stay open' and breaks M4's client, which sends no token on list(). Whoever takes this needs to decide (a) or (b) with the integrator first, because (a) is a contract change and (b) is an API change. Doing half — coarsening the field while the sweeper still needs seconds — breaks the sweeper and leaves the channel open through ?since= anyway. Analysis is written up in infra/relay/README.md under 'Known gap'.

L4.note: DONE in PR #61, alongside M11 — because M11 made ask reachable, which made this defect live rather than theoretical. Linted at the boundary in ask.ts rather than in template.ts, because both narrators consume facts.inducedClaim and only the source covers both. Dropped rather than scrubbed: a claim that failed the linter is one we do not understand well enough to edit. Two checks — K5's lexicon, plus a raw-identifier shape test, since an enum token is not a banned WORD.

M13.title: Trust nothing about search params: the API accepts unknown fields with 200, so episode_slots may be a no-op — do the reservation client-side (R3)
M13.note: MEASURED and fixed. NO search parameter is honored: top_k=1 returns 13 rows; episode_slots=0 and 99 are indistinguishable; limit/size/max_results/n/per_page and every type filter are inert too, all with 200. The prior reasoning in pool.ts and user.ts ('top-k headroom is what actually protects the claim') was FALSE, not merely unproven, and the constants carrying it are deleted. Second measurement is the useful one: the IDENTICAL request returns 13/3E 13/3E 11/2E 13/3E 13/3E 11/2E, so the search is non-deterministic and an empty answer is not an empty scope. Reservation is now client-side in src/memory/episodes.ts: bounded retry (3) for an episode, never for facts, logged so a thin claim is attributable. Parameters still sent - inert but forward-compatible. Caution for the next probe: k=3 returned 7 rows once and looked like the real parameter name; repeating six times showed it was non-determinism.

M14.title: Pool ingests as prose, not JSON (guide R4) — ships WITH M12's conv_id batching; neither half works alone
M14.note: DONE with M12 in PR #60. src/memory/readProse.ts renders a read as two third-person English sentences with place NAMES; refuses to emit an id for an unknown place rather than falling back. Every possible sentence (signals x drivers x cadences) is linted by K5 in readProse.test.ts, because whatever goes into the pool can come back out onto a card. Measured effect: batching alone still leaked 3 identifier-carrying texts; batching + prose leaked 0.

M15.title: Adopting M12/M14 needs a clean pool scope: pre-M12 per-read episodes outrank the new cross-record ones
M15.note: Built. Moved to generation-marked scopes (SCOPE_GENERATION=v2) rather than purging, per the owner's decision. BOTH scopes: confit:pool:v2 and confit:user:v2:<profile> (the personal scope was the bare profile id, which is why it had no way out of its own history). Settings are unaffected - they live on the relay under D-8 keys, which is what makes a future bump cheap. Guard globs src/** at source level plus behavioural assertions; red-verified against three mutations. OPERATIONAL half done live: 220 reads seeded into the new pool scope as 17 conversations, 0 failed. Old records remain and still cost quota (GET /v1/usage); a purge stays available later and by then nothing depends on the old scope.

M16.title: The Ask reads all three D-8 inputs: add the PERSONAL synthesis, which is written today and never read
M16.note: DONE in PR #64. UserStore.personalClaim mirrors M2's inducedClaim over the user's own scope; NarratorFacts.inducedClaim split into poolClaim + personalClaim; Card/CardCopy gained personalLine; both claims share ONE lint gate. Not model-generated in either narrator — a fixed catalog frame, because a third layer of paraphrase on a claim about the reader is where drift matters most. No floor per the owner's ruling, with episode/fact counts logged so a thin claim is attributable. VERIFIED LIVE and the measurement matters more than the feature: the claim is ONE confession, not seven, because writeProse mints a fresh conv_id per call (18 rows, 8 episodes, 8 distinct conv_ids) — the M12 defect in the personal tier. AND the obvious fix fails: 4 separate POSTs sharing one conv_id still gave per-POST paraphrases, so episodes are generated per INGEST CALL not per accumulated conversation. Cross-confession synthesis needs M17's spool. Registered as M20.

M17.title: Durable confession spool: verify prose is RETRIEVABLE, not merely 'complete', and re-ingest what XTrace dropped
M17.note: CLOSED BY DECISION D-10, not built. The owner ruled that losing a confession is acceptable, which removes the motivation: a spool sized for a DELIVERY GUARANTEE (atomic writes, retrievability verification, stuck-item escalation) is machinery for a promise nobody wants to make. What survives moved into M20, which needs only a buffer — losing it is explicitly fine, so no atomicity, no verification, no escalation. NOTE: surfacing result.memories_created[] was going to fall out of this task's verification work; with M17 closed it does not, so M10 (the ingest ledger) stays fully independent and still needs the client change.

P0.10.title: SL-06: import KFLOOR into frozen contracts stub instead of a second copy, and floor StubNarrator's citation
P0.10.note: Fixed. Stub imports KFLOOR; StubNarrator floors its citation like TemplateNarrator. Guarded through the stubs behaviour, red-verified against both mutations.

P0.11.title: SL-07: infra/relay/server.ts reimplements parseRead instead of importing it
P0.11.note: SL-07 in docs/defect-log.md (still open). infra/relay/server.ts:24-56 has a 32-line validateRead() duplicating src/kernel/read.ts's parseRead(), with error strings already diverging. Fix: import parseRead and make validateRead a thin try/catch adapter.

P0.12.title: SL-08: delete or replace the unimplementable AskEngine contract interface
P0.12.note: AskEngine DELETED, not re-specced: a Card carries narrated copy and copy needs a model call, so no synchronous pure function can return one. The stub plus its contract test formed a closed loop that agreed with itself while nothing real could comply. modules.ts now names the real seam (planAsk + assembleCard) and a test asserts the interface stays gone.

M18.title: SL-14: URL(...).pathname used as a filesystem path breaks on spaced checkouts
M18.note: SL-14 in docs/defect-log.md (still open). scripts/seed/load-seeds.ts:45 (and originally src/memory/poolView.ts:30, may already be fixed there — check) build a path via new URL(...).pathname, which URL-encodes spaces as %20 and is not a valid fs path. Use fileURLToPath(new URL(...)) from node:url instead.

S5.title: SL-17: induction-set.json is a byte-identical copy of reads.json, so the pass census cross-check reports clean with XTrace unreachable
S5.note: SL-17 in docs/defect-log.md (still open). data/seeds/induction-set.json must be derived from what actually landed in XTrace via induction (S2's own induced claims), not a copy of the raw seed reads — otherwise confit pass census's [E22] cross-check can never catch a broken pool.

X8.title: SL-16: census labels the six UNMATCHABLE_DRIVERS citable
X8.note: SL-16 in docs/defect-log.md (still open). src/cli/pass-report.ts's citable check is k >= KFLOOR only; it does not exclude UNMATCHABLE_DRIVERS (the drivers D-5 proved can never reach a card). Six of eleven census rows are wrong.

X9.title: SL-19: confit forget prints "Deleted from Confit" when a target was only skipped
X9.note: SL-19 in docs/defect-log.md (still open). src/cli/forget.ts headline() treats any single target reaching status 'deleted' as sufficient to claim overall deletion, even when another target (e.g. user tier) is 'skipped'. Its own test locks the overclaim in — fix headline() and forget.test.ts together.

X10.note: SL-20 in docs/defect-log.md (still open). src/cli/pass-report.ts's neartie output prints raw 'weight' and 'score' words, which are in K5's banned lexicon. No CLI line in the product is ever copy-linted; this is the reproduction case.

N2.title: SL-23: NudgeState is never persisted anywhere
N2.note: Released unstarted: the real fix needs SettingsStore threaded onto AdapterGraph (src/config/wiring.ts, both liveGraph and fixtureGraph) since nudge state has no natural per-profile scope today (pass nudge --arm takes no --profile) — a design call (which scope key to persist under) plus a wiring change in a file another concurrent session is actively iterating on (M11/M19 touched wiring.ts and the settings store this same session). Left for a session that can coordinate on the wiring change rather than risk a collision.

M19.title: Allergies have a durable home and no field to put them in: UsualProfile has no allergy, and offLimits does not filter recommendations
M19.note: CLOSED BY DECISION D-9, not built — the product owner chose option (c): do not claim allergy filtering, and say so. The premise check is why: data/places.json carries SIX place tags across 40 records and none is an allergen; Place has no ingredient field (signatureDishes is spiceLevel only); PlaceTag is a closed union enforced by the type AND validate-corpus.ts. So there was nothing to filter on. Shipped instead: the disclaimer in the two places a user forms a belief (the editor where they type 'shellfish', the refusal where they learn the feature exists), a safety claim REMOVED from M14's pool prose ('genuinely unsafe' was measured coming back out of the live API as a card-bound induced claim), and tests/guards/safetyClaims.test.ts which asserts the tag set so adding an allergen tag later reopens this decision. If option (a) is ever wanted: UsualProfile contract change + PlaceTag contract change + re-audit of all 40 corpus records, where a place mistagged as allergen-free is the exact failure the feature would exist to prevent and no test can catch it.

K8.title: budgetBand is both a hard veto and a soft fit — inconsistent with D-8's 'soft preferences on similar footing to evidence'
K8.note: Merged as #69 (58a4968). D-11 in the DAG. Lift gated on matched() at KFLOOR with [E20] dedup; polarity unconsulted by design; gi hard. Demo candidate sets unchanged under committed seeds; 913/913.

M20.title: Personal synthesis is per-confession, not cross-confession: episodes are generated per INGEST CALL, so a stable conv_id is not enough
M20.note: Built and pushed. Batching verified live: 4 confessions produced 1 conv_id and 1 episode synthesising all four (was 8 confessions, 8 episodes, 8 conv_ids). Buffer is local, plain writeFileSync, clears before the caller ingests -- the loss D-10 sanctions. Dead verifyPendingProse/dropUnconfirmedProse deleted (no production caller, and they cleared on job completion rather than memory survival). confess receipt now distinguishes held from sent. offLimits guard hardened: batching had made its zero-row assertion tautological. Gate green except gate zero, which is blocked by design on G7.

L5.title: The card is now too long: with all three D-8 inputs live, the reason line alone is a 17-place paragraph
L5.note: Emerged from having D-8's three inputs working at once, which nothing had seen before. A live card now runs: a reason line that names SEVENTEEN places in one paragraph (the pool claim, interpolated into reason_induced_cited), a cohort-miss line, a rotation line, a usual line, and a four-sentence personal claim. Roughly 200 words where design v0.8 §5 specifies four lines. Neither claim is ours to rewrite — both are XTrace synthesis — so this is a LENGTH and SELECTION problem, not a copy-quality one: decide how much substrate prose a card may carry, and where it is truncated or summarised. Note the substrate's episode register leaks through both ('The conversation centered on...', 'The session ended by reinforcing...'), which reads as a transcript summary rather than a recommendation. Do NOT fix by sending the claim to a model to shorten — that adds a third layer of paraphrase to text already twice-removed from the user's words, and the personal claim is where drift matters most (see the withPersonalLine note in src/llm/narrator.ts).
